title: Wave motion and energy transfer practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: Questions use new contexts and wording while testing the mapped definition and wave-property demands.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by a progressive wave.
A pulse travels along a rope past a small painted mark. Which observation best describes the painted mark after the complete pulse has passed?

options.A: It has travelled to the far end with the pulse.
options.B: It has moved briefly and returned near its equilibrium position.
options.C: It has remained completely at rest.
options.D: It has moved steadily in the direction opposite to the pulse.

questions.prompt: Circular ripples spread across a tank and make a floating leaf move. What is transferred from the source to the leaf by the ripples?

options.C: Both energy and a net amount of water

questions.prompt: A compressed region travels along a stretched spring. Which statement correctly separates the disturbance from the spring coils?

options.A: The disturbance and every coil travel together to the far end.
options.B: The disturbance stays fixed while all coils travel along the spring.
options.C: The disturbance travels while individual coils move locally and return.
options.D: Neither the disturbance nor the coils move.

questions.prompt: A student flicks one end of a rope. A single pulse travels to a light ring attached at the far end and makes the ring move.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Identify the observation that shows energy has reached the far end.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the pulse can reach the ring even though each small section of rope remains near its original position.

questions.prompt: A cork floats on a ripple tank. Straight ripples travel from a paddle on the left to an absorber on the right.

figure.purpose: Require learners to distinguish the ripple route from the local motion of a marked cork.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired line diagram, top view, with paddle, three straight ripple fronts, cork and absorber. Include no motion arrows or answer labels.
figure.alt_text: A top-view ripple tank has a paddle on the left, straight ripple fronts, a cork in the middle and an absorber on the right.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe separately the motion of the ripples and the motion of the cork.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The absorber begins to vibrate when the ripples arrive. Explain what this shows about the ripples.

questions.prompt: Three equally spaced beads are fixed to a long rope. A short pulse is sent from left to right. The sketches show the rope at three successive times.

figure.purpose: Assess interpretation of a travelling pattern and local material motion across a time sequence.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white Cambridge-inspired three-frame rope sequence. Show the same labelled beads P, Q and R, with the pulse successively near each bead. Do not include arrows or trajectories.
figure.alt_text: Three successive rope sketches show one pulse travelling past fixed labelled beads P, Q and R.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Compare the movement of bead Q with the movement of the pulse.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how energy reaches bead R without bead P travelling to R.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State one observation that would contradict the claim that the rope material travels with the pulse.
